name: ocmtoc
why: Converting Mach-O binaries to PE/COFF is a curious format transform, though its niche is narrow and the idea is only half-explored here.

brief.what_it_is: ocmtoc is a converter that takes Mach-O binaries (the executable format used on macOS) and produces PE binaries, the Windows executable format, which also covers PE/COFF output. The brew metadata names its executable as mtoc. The README is a single short paragraph and does not describe inputs, output options, or usage, so the details of the conversion beyond this are unknown from the page.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no stated motivation. It only says the tool is used in Acidanthera UDK and EDK II, which suggests it exists to support UEFI firmware development, where Mach-O-built code has to end up as PE images.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no installation steps, dependencies, or first-run setup beyond the Homebrew formula metadata, which lists the executable as mtoc.
brief.standout: It is a niche format converter whose main visible use is inside two firmware toolchains (Acidanthera UDK and EDK II) rather than as a standalone end-user tool. The README does not explain the technique, so nothing about how it is cleverer than similar tools can be confirmed from this page.
brief.status: unknown. The README has a GitHub Actions build badge for the master branch, but the page I fetched did not show its result, and there is no release date, last-commit date, or maintenance note in the README.
brief.caveats: The README is very thin: one descriptive line, a build badge, and no usage, limitations, platform notes, or license information. The scout note calls the idea 'only half-explored', which is an opinion and not something the README supports. Only the homepage was fetched; no docs were linked from the README, so none were followed.
quotes: Mach-O to PE converter used in Acidanthera UDK and EDK II.
